problem_markdown: Let $A,B$ be adjacent vertices of a regular $n$-gon with centre $O$, where $n\ge5$. A rigid triangle $XYZ$, initially $OAB$, moves continuously with $Y,Z$ on the polygon boundary, each traversing that boundary, and $X$ inside. Determine the locus of $X$.
solutions_markdown:
Let the polygon side be $s$, circumradius $R$, and $\alpha=\pi/n$. The locus is the union of $n$ radial segments beginning at $O$, each directed away from a polygon vertex, of length $R(\sec\alpha-1)$.

Scale $s$ to two. Two boundary points at distance two can lie on the same side only as its endpoints; otherwise they are on adjacent sides. For nonadjacent sides, take their shorter boundary chain and project onto its central direction: that of the middle intervening side, or halfway between the two middle directions. The end segments and all intervening sides have nonnegative projection. A single middle side contributes two; two middle sides contribute $4\cos\alpha>2$. Equality can occur only at the nearest endpoints of sides separated by one side. Thus no other nonadjacent positions have distance two.

During a transition about a vertex $V$, choose coordinates with $V=(0,0)$ and its inward bisector the positive vertical axis. Write
$$Y=p(-\cos\alpha,\sin\alpha),\quad Z=q(\cos\alpha,\sin\alpha),\quad0\le p,q\le2.$$
The fixed-base constraint is
$$4=(p+q)^2\cos^2\alpha+(p-q)^2\sin^2\alpha.$$
The inward apex of the congruent triangle is $X=(0,(p+q)/(2\sin\alpha))$. Along the continuous transition, $p+q$ runs from 2 to $2\sec\alpha$ and back to 2. Since $O=(0,\csc\alpha)$, this traces exactly the claimed segment. Its far endpoint remains inside the polygon because $\sec\alpha-1<\cos\alpha$ for $\alpha\le\pi/5$, placing the segment within the incircle. The other vertices give the rotated segments. Restoring scale gives the displayed length.
